title: The Mismatch Moment — Setting Up the Problem You Will Solve
course: Why Your GROUP BY Total Doesn't Match the Dashboard

events.narration: Hey, welcome. This lesson's for you if you've just started writing S-Q-L, or maybe you've recently landed your first data analyst gig and you're staring at a query result that doesn't match what the dashboard says. By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to describe exactly how a perfectly correct GROUP BY query can still give you the wrong total, and you'll know the five root-cause categories we're going to investigate together across this course. Let's jump in.

Alright, here's our database. We've got two tables. First, the orders table, with columns order ID, order date, customer name, region, and order total. That's the raw transactional data, every sale that went through the system. Second, we've got a dashboard snapshot table, with columns region, reported total, and snapshot date. Think of this as a frozen copy of what the dashboard showed at a particular moment in time. Two tables, supposedly telling the same story. Let's see if they agree.

Here's our first query. It's about as simple as S-Q-L gets. We're summing order total from the orders table, grouped by region. No filters, no joins, no fancy window functions. Just, hey database, tell me the total for each region. This is the kind of query you'd write on day one. Let's run it.

Three rows back, one per region. Northeast comes in at fifteen thousand two hundred forty-one point two zero, with five orders. South shows eleven thousand eleven point five zero across four orders. And West lands at twelve thousand nine hundred five point seven five, also four orders. Looks clean. Looks right. No errors, no warnings. You'd feel pretty good about this, right? Yeah. Hold that thought.

Now here's where things get interesting. This next query pulls the reported totals from the dashboard snapshot table and lines them up against our live totals from the orders table. Same regions, side by side, with a gap column showing the difference. This is the moment of truth. Let's run it and see if the numbers agree.

Ooof. Every single region is off. Northeast, the dashboard says twelve thousand three hundred sixty-five point eight zero, but our live query says fifteen thousand two hundred forty-one point two zero. That's a gap of two thousand eight hundred seventy-five point four zero. The West is even worse, a gap of three thousand three hundred ten point zero zero. And the South's off by one thousand nine hundred sixty point two five. Not one region matches. This is exactly the kind of moment where you get that Slack message from your manager saying, hey, your numbers don't match the dashboard, what's going on?

So let's play detective. This next query pulls out the specific orders that are causing the gap, the ones that exist in the orders table but weren't included when the dashboard snapshot was taken. Let's see who the culprits are.

Three orders. That's it, just three rows causing all this chaos. Order one zero one one, placed on March fifteenth twenty twenty-four by Northwind Traders in the Northeast, order total two thousand eight hundred seventy-five point four zero. Hey, that matches the Northeast gap exactly. Then we've got order one zero one two from Coastal Dynamics out West, three thousand three hundred ten point zero zero, which is the West's gap to the penny. And order one zero one three from Delta Farms Inc in the South, one thousand nine hundred sixty point two five, matching the South's gap perfectly. Three late-arriving orders that the dashboard snapshot didn't capture, but our live query picked up. Mystery solved, at least for this one.

And just to prove we're not making this up, here's a query that excludes those three orders and recalculates the totals. If our detective work is right, these corrected numbers should match the dashboard snapshot exactly. Let's see.

There it is. Northeast, twelve thousand three hundred sixty-five point eight zero. South, nine thousand fifty-one point two five. West, nine thousand five hundred ninety-five point seven five. Every single one matches the dashboard snapshot. The alibi checks out. Our S-Q-L wasn't wrong, it was just including data the dashboard hadn't seen yet.

So here's your takeaway. A syntactically perfect GROUP BY query can still return totals that don't match the dashboard, and the problem is almost never the S-Q-L engine itself. It's a mismatch between what your query includes and what the dashboard includes. In this case, it was timing, orders that arrived after the snapshot. But across this course, we're going to dig into four more root causes, duplicate rows inflating your totals, filter mismatches where your query and the dashboard aren't looking at the same slice of data, NULL handling where missing values silently skew your aggregations, and date or timezone logic where the same order lands on different days depending on who's asking. Five causes, five lessons, and by the end you'll have a reusable checklist you can pull out any time a number doesn't match. Let's get started with the most common culprit, duplicate rows.
